name: Wheatgrass
short: Worsened nausea made six patients on breast cancer chemotherapy stop wheatgrass juice (small study). Other small studies reported no serious adverse effects.
text: Safety data come from small studies of wheatgrass juice or tablets taken by mouth. In a matched-control study of patients receiving chemotherapy for breast cancer (60 enrolled across the wheatgrass and control arms), side effects of wheatgrass juice were called minimal by the authors, but worsening nausea led six patients in the wheatgrass arm to stop taking it. A 1-month placebo-controlled trial of daily wheatgrass juice in 23 patients with active distal ulcerative colitis found no serious side effects, and in uncontrolled studies in patients with beta thalassaemia major (16 using home-grown juice; 53 using tablets for a year) no adverse effects were noted. A 2015 review reported that no adverse events of wheatgrass had been reported, although some forms pose problems of tolerability, and noted that all trials were small with methodological problems. The abstracts do not report on pregnancy or longer-term use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
